summary: The US Justice Department's PATTERN tool, used to decide which federal prisoners qualify for early release, produced uneven results by race. It overpredicted risk for many Black, Hispanic and Asian people, leaving some in prison who might otherwise qualify.
technical_summary: PATTERN is an algorithmic recidivism risk assessment used to determine First Step Act early-release eligibility. DOJ's own review found differential prediction error across racial groups, with overprediction of general risk and underprediction of violent risk for some inmates of color, producing disparate risk classifications.

sector.quote: Only inmates who pose a low or minimal risk of returning to crime can qualify for the programs

technology.quote: overpredicted the risk that many Black, Hispanic and Asian people would commit new crimes

failure_mode.quote: persistent racial disparities that put Black and brown people at a disadvantage

affected_population.quote: persistent racial disparities that put Black and brown people at a disadvantage

notes: Harm is potential denial of early release; individual outcomes not documented in excerpt.

summary: Three major Australian retailers were reported to be analysing in-store camera footage to build facial profiles of customers, including children, without their knowledge. A consumer group said this may breach privacy law and regulators opened investigations.
technical_summary: Facial recognition applied to CCTV footage in retail stores created biometric faceprints of shoppers. Retailers cited loss prevention and safety, but notice was limited to discreet signage and privacy policies, so customers did not meaningfully consent to biometric collection.

sector.quote: Major Australian retailers have been secretly capturing the faces of their customers without their knowledge

technology.quote: Kmart, Bunnings and The Good Guys are using facial recognition technology in stores

failure_mode.quote: analysing CCTV footage to create profiles or “face prints” of their customers, including children, without their knowledge

harm_type.quote: analysing CCTV footage to create profiles or “face prints” of their customers, including children, without their knowledge

affected_population.quote: analysing CCTV footage to create profiles or “face prints” of their customers, including children, without their knowledge
analysing CCTV footage to create profiles or “face prints” of their customers, including children, without their knowledge

notes: Retailers dispute that the practice breached the Privacy Act; regulator investigations were opened.

summary: California's motor vehicle regulator accused Tesla of false advertising, saying the names and descriptions of Autopilot and Full Self-Driving made the driver-assist features sound more capable than they are.
technical_summary: Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving are driver-assistance (ADAS) features requiring active supervision. The regulator alleges branding and website copy implied autonomy, creating a mismatch between perceived and actual capability that risks overreliance and misleads buyers.

affected_population.quote: misled customers with advertising language on its website describing Autopilot and Full Self-Driving technologies as more capable than they actually are

notes: Allegations by the DMV, not findings; no specific injury is described in the excerpts.

summary: An Uber self-driving test vehicle struck and killed a woman crossing a street in Tempe, Arizona. Investigators reported the emergency braking was disabled and the safety driver was streaming video.
technical_summary: An Uber-modified Volvo SUV in autonomous mode detected the pedestrian but did not brake because automated emergency braking was disabled during computer control. The human safety driver, relied on to intervene, was distracted by a phone and was not alerted in time.

technology.quote: A 49-year-old woman was hit and killed by a self-driving Volvo operated by Uber while crossing a street in Tempe

failure_mode.quote: the emergency braking maneuvers were disabled whilst the car was being controlled by a computer

severity.quote: A 49-year-old woman was hit and killed by a self-driving Volvo operated by Uber while crossing a street in Tempe

notes: Both system design (disabled braking) and safety-driver distraction are presented as causes.

summary: Wikipedia's automated editing bots, each built to improve the encyclopedia, got locked in long-running loops of undoing one another's edits. A study found some of these conflicts lasted for years.
technical_summary: Independent rule-based bots on Wikipedia made conflicting edits, such as reverting links or corrections, and reverted each other repeatedly. With no coordination or conflict detection between bots, simple automated rules produced persistent feedback loops across many language editions.

failure_mode.quote: The more the bots came into contact with one another, the more they became locked in combat, undoing each other’s edits

notes: No concrete harm to people is reported; harm is wasted effort and edit instability.

summary: The Chinese government used AI-enabled surveillance, including facial recognition and a policing data platform, to monitor and target Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in Xinjiang. Flagged people could be detained.
technical_summary: An integrated surveillance ecosystem, including the IJOP platform and a police mobile app, aggregates personal data from cameras, biometrics and other sources and flags people deemed suspicious for investigation or detention. It enables mass, discriminatory social control of an ethnic and religious minority.

sector.quote: mobile app that police and other officials use to communicate with the Integrated Joint Operations Platform

technology.quote: the policing program aggregates data about people and flags to officials those it deems potentially threatening

failure_mode.quote: authorities are collecting massive amounts of personal information

harm_type.quote: subjected the 13 million ethnic Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims in Xinjiang to mass arbitrary detention

affected_population.quote: subjected the 13 million ethnic Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims in Xinjiang to mass arbitrary detention
subjected the 13 million ethnic Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims in Xinjiang to mass arbitrary detention

severity.quote: up to one million people are being held in “political education” camps

notes: Severity rests on HRW-cited estimates of detentions; attribution to AI systems versus wider state policy is mixed.

summary: An image upscaling tool called PULSE turned pixelated photos of people of color, including well-known public figures, into faces with white features. The outputs were widely shared as an example of racial bias in AI.
technical_summary: PULSE uses NVIDIA's StyleGAN to generate a high-resolution face that downsamples to the input image. Outputs skewed toward Caucasian features for low-resolution photos of people of color. Experts disagreed whether the bias came from StyleGAN's training data or the PULSE search method.

technology.quote: The program generating these images is an algorithm called PULSE, which uses a technique known as upscaling to process visual data

failure_mode.quote: the tool struggles when the obscured photos feature people of colour since it often chooses fake images of people that are white

affected_population.quote: the tool struggles when the obscured photos feature people of colour since it often chooses fake images of people that are white

notes: Source of bias (StyleGAN data versus PULSE method) was disputed among experts.

summary: A climate action group released a deepfake video of Belgium's prime minister appearing to link the Covid-19 pandemic to the ecological crisis and call for change. The speech was fabricated.
technical_summary: Machine learning was used to alter an authentic televised address, reproducing the prime minister's voice and likeness so that she appeared to deliver a fabricated climate speech. It was published online and sent to government offices.

technology.quote: A deepfake video showing Belgium’s prime minister speaking of an urgent need to tackle the economic and climate crises

affected_population.quote: machine learning and artificial technology to reproduce Wilmès’ voice and likeness

notes: Advocacy deepfake with a benign stated aim; coded as misuse because it fabricated a public official's speech.

summary: Sexually explicit AI-generated images of Taylor Swift spread on X, with one post seen more than 45 million times before removal. The images reportedly came from a Telegram group and prompted outrage and temporary search blocks.
technical_summary: Users generated non-consensual explicit deepfakes of a real person with AI image generators, reportedly including Microsoft Designer, and posted them on X. The platform's moderation was slow to detect and remove the content despite policies banning it, and posts spread widely before takedown.

summary: An AI-generated song imitating the voices of Drake and The Weeknd went viral and was then removed from major streaming services after their music publisher said it violated copyright.
technical_summary: Generative voice cloning produced vocals mimicking two recording artists on an original track. The publisher alleged that training on the artists' music and distribution of the output infringed copyright, leading to takedowns from streaming and video platforms.

summary: A crypto bug bounty platform banned 15 users who submitted bug reports written by ChatGPT. The platform said the reports looked convincing but were nonsense and wasted staff and project time.
technical_summary: Users prompted ChatGPT to generate vulnerability reports for smart contracts. The text was fluent and well-structured but had no real relation to the projects' code, a hallucination-style failure of a general language model used outside its capability for technical analysis.

technology.quote: bug reports created by the generative artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT

failure_mode.quote: you are using a single prompt to generate something that looks like a well-written bug report, but is nonsense when analyzed further

harm_type.quote: This wastes the white hat’s time, Immunefi’s time and the projects’ time.

notes: Both the model's output and users' decision to submit it unvetted contributed.

summary: SoftBank's humanoid robot Pepper reportedly kept failing at real jobs, including mechanical errors, unplanned breaks and not recognizing people it had met. Some customers ended their contracts.
technical_summary: Pepper, a humanoid service robot, suffered mechanical errors, unplanned breaks, failures to recognize people and breakdowns during practice runs when deployed in roles such as funeral services and nursing homes. Its human form raised expectations beyond its actual capabilities.

technology.quote: the robot, made by SoftBank Group Corp., kept breaking down during practice runs

failure_mode.quote: The robots have been prone to mechanical errors and unplanned breaks

notes: Harm is limited to business disruption and lost contracts.
